cli.browser_node.heading_dry_run: Node browser on {node} — dry run, nothing was changed:
cli.browser_node.heading_uninstall_dry_r: Removing the node browser from {node} — dry run, nothing was changed:
cli.browser_node.step_skipped: {step}: skipped, because an earlier step failed
cli.browser_node.refuse_platform: Refused: the node-managed browser supports Linux on x86_64 only; this is {system} {machine}.
cli.browser_node.refuse_distro: Refused: the node-managed browser needs a dnf/rpm distribution (Amazon Linux 2023, Fedora or the RHEL family).
cli.browser_node.refuse_user_machine: Refused: this is a user's machine ({reason}). On a user's machine the browser tool drives that person's own Chrome through the extension or the desktop app — see guide://browser.
cli.browser_node.refuse_not_member: Refused: this device is not in a lop mesh network. Join one first (guide://network), then run this again.
cli.browser_node.refuse_sudo: Refused: these steps need root and `sudo -n` would prompt: {steps}. Run it from an account with non-interactive sudo; or, at an interactive terminal, run `sudo -v` first and then this command again in the same terminal (guide://browser, "Headless nodes").
cli.browser_node.refuse_no_record: Refused: there is nothing to repair, because {path} does not exist. Install it with `lop browser setup --node --authorised-by '<who, when>'`.
cli.browser_node.refuse_authorisation: Refused: installing a browser on a node needs the operator's authorisation. Run it again with `--authorised-by '<who, when>'`; the text is recorded verbatim.
cli.browser_node.paired_yes: Paired: yes. New sessions on this node get the browser tool (sessions already running do not), but no site can be opened there yet: per-site approval on a headless node needs the operator's signed decision, which this build does not have.
cli.browser_node.failed_tail: Setup stopped at the failed step. Fix it, then run `lop browser setup --node --repair --authorised-by '<who, when>'`.
cli.browser_node.help_setup: Set up the node-managed browser on a headless mesh node
cli.browser_node.help_node: Install the node-managed headless Chrome (headless mesh nodes only)
cli.browser_node.help_dry_run: Show every step and whether it is already in place; change nothing
cli.browser_node.help_repair: Re-apply only the steps that are no longer in place on an existing install
cli.browser_node.help_upgrade: Move the pinned Chrome and the extension to their newest verified versions
cli.browser_node.help_extension_dir: Pack this built extension directory instead of the newest GitHub Release asset
cli.browser_node.help_authorised_by: Who authorised this, and when; recorded verbatim (required unless --dry-run)
cli.browser_node.help_uninstall_node: Remove the node-managed browser (unit, policy, version lock, Chrome package)
cli.browser_node.uninstall_kept: Kept: the extension signing key (so a reinstall keeps the same extension id), Google's imported signing key, the fonts, the bridge daemon and the install record.
cli.browser_node.refuse_uninstall_author: Refused: removing the node browser needs the operator's authorisation. Run it again with `--authorised-by '<who, when>'`; the text is recorded verbatim.
cli.browser_node.refuse_nothing_to_unins: Refused: {path} records no node browser that lop installed, so there is nothing of lop's to remove. A browser installed some other way is not lop's to remove.
cli.browser_node.dry_run_would_fail: Setup would not complete as things stand: fix the rows marked "would fail" first.
cli.browser_node.stopped_unchanged: Nothing was changed. Fix the failed step, then run the same command again.
cli.browser_node.setup_needs_node: `lop browser setup` needs --node and is for headless mesh nodes only: try `lop browser setup --node --dry-run`. On your own machine, use `lop browser install`.
cli.browser_node.purge_with_node: --purge does not apply with --node: the node uninstall keeps the bridge daemon and its pairing state. To remove those too, run `lop browser uninstall --purge` afterwards.
cli.browser_node.uninstall_flags_need_no: --dry-run, --authorised-by and --json apply only to `lop browser uninstall --node`; nothing was removed.
